sanskrit: rāmo 'pi rātriśeṣeṇa tenaiva mahad antaram jagāma puruṣavyāghraḥ pitur ājñām anusmaran
english: Rāma too, that tiger among men, keeping his father's command ever in mind, covered a great distance through the remaining hours of the night.

sanskrit: tathaiva gacchatas tasya vyapāyād rajanī śivā upāsya sa śivāṃ saṃdhyāṃ viṣayāntaṃ vyagāhata
english: As he journeyed on in this way, the auspicious night passed away; having duly observed the auspicious twilight rite, he pressed onward to the border of the realm.

sanskrit: grāmān vikṛṣṭasīmāṃs tān puṣpitāni vanāni ca paśyann atiyayau śīghraṃ śarair iva hayottamaiḥ
english: Beholding villages with their far-flung boundaries and flowering forests, he sped swiftly past, as if borne by arrows, on those excellent horses.

sanskrit: śṛṇvan vāco manuṣyāṇāṃ grāmasaṃvāsavāsinām rājānaṃ dhig daśarathaṃ kāmasya vaśam āgatam
english: He heard the words of the people dwelling in the villages along the way: "Shame on King Daśaratha, who has fallen under the sway of desire!"

sanskrit: hā nṛśaṃsādya kaikeyī pāpā pāpānubandhinī tīkṣṇā saṃbhinnamaryādā tīkṣṇe karmaṇi vartate
english: "Alas, how cruel is Kaikeyī today — wicked, ever trailing wickedness, harsh, one who has shattered all propriety and pursues a terrible deed!"

sanskrit: yā putram īdṛśaṃ rājñaḥ pravāsayati dhārmikam vana vāse mahāprājñaṃ sānukrośam atandritam
english: "She who sends away into forest exile such a son of the king — righteous, supremely wise, compassionate, and ever diligent!"

sanskrit: etā vāco manuṣyāṇāṃ grāmasaṃvāsavāsinām śṛṇvann atiyayau vīraḥ kosalān kosaleśvaraḥ
english: Hearing these words of the people who dwelt in the villages, that hero, the lord of the Kosalas, passed beyond the land of Kosala.

sanskrit: tato vedaśrutiṃ nāma śivavārivahāṃ nadīm uttīryābhimukhaḥ prāyād agastyādhyuṣitāṃ diśam
english: Then, having crossed the river named Vedaśruti, whose waters are auspicious and wholesome, he set out toward the quarter once inhabited by the sage Agastya.

sanskrit: gatvā tu suciraṃ kālaṃ tataḥ śītajalāṃ nadīm gomatīṃ goyutānūpām atarat sāgaraṃgamām
english: Having traveled for a long while, he then crossed the river Gomatī, whose waters are cool, whose banks are rich with cattle and meadows, and which flows down to the ocean.

sanskrit: gomatīṃ cāpy atikramya rāghavaḥ śīghragair hayaiḥ mayūrahaṃsābhirutāṃ tatāra syandikāṃ nadīm
english: And having passed beyond the Gomatī, Rāghava, with his swift-footed horses, crossed the river Syandikā, which resounds with the cries of peacocks and geese.

sanskrit: sa mahīṃ manunā rājñā dattām ikṣvākave purā sphītāṃ rāṣṭrāvṛtāṃ rāmo vaidehīm anvadarśayat
english: Rāma pointed out to Vaidehī that prosperous land, encircled by the kingdom, which was once granted to Ikṣvāku by King Manu in the days of old.

sanskrit: sūta ity eva cābhāṣya sārathiṃ tam abhīkṣṇaśaḥ haṃsamattasvaraḥ śrīmān uvāca puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Repeatedly addressing the charioteer as "sūta," that glorious bull among men, his voice deep and resonant as a swan in rut, spoke thus:

sanskrit: kadāhaṃ punar āgamya sarayvāḥ puṣpite vane mṛgayāṃ paryāṭaṣyāmi mātrā pitrā ca saṃgataḥ
english: "When shall I come back again and roam in sport through the flowering forest along the Sarayū, reunited with my mother and my father?"

sanskrit: nātyartham abhikāṅkṣāmi mṛgayāṃ sarayūvane ratir hy eṣātulā loke rājarṣigaṇasaṃmatā
english: "I do not overly crave the hunt in the forest of the Sarayū — yet this pleasure is peerless in the world and is esteemed by the assemblies of royal sages."

sanskrit: sa tam adhvānam aikṣvākaḥ sūtaṃ madhurayā girā taṃ tam artham abhipretya yayauvākyam udīrayan
english: Thus that scion of Ikṣvāku journeyed on, addressing his charioteer in a sweet voice, speaking one thought after another as each came to his mind.

sanskrit: viśālān kosalān ramyān yātvā lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ āsasāda mahābāhuḥ śṛṅgaverapuraṃ prati
english: Having traversed the wide and lovely lands of Kosala, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, that mighty-armed one, drew near to the city of Śṛṅgaverapura.

sanskrit: tatra tripathagāṃ divyāṃ śivatoyām aśaivalām dadarśa rāghavo gaṅgāṃ puṇyām ṛṣinisevitām
english: There Rāghava beheld the divine Gaṅgā, flowing across three paths, her waters auspicious and free of algae, holy and frequented by sages.

sanskrit: haṃsasārasasaṃghuṣṭāṃ cakravākopakūjitām śiṃśumaraiś ca nakraiś ca bhujaṃgaiś ca niṣevitām
english: She was filled with the clamor of swans and sāras cranes, the cooing of cakravāka birds; she was frequented by śiṃśumāra dolphins, crocodiles, and serpents.

sanskrit: tām ūrmikalilāvartām anvavekṣya mahārathaḥ sumantram abravīt sūtam ihaivādya vasāmahe
english: Gazing upon her, swirling with eddies set in motion by her waves, that great warrior spoke to the charioteer Sumantra: "Here we shall encamp today."

sanskrit: avidūrād ayaṃ nadyā bahupuṣpapravālavān sumahān iṅgudīvṛkṣo vasāmo 'traiva sārathe
english: "Not far from the river stands this great iṅgudī tree, laden with many blossoms and tender shoots — let us stay right here, O charioteer."

sanskrit: lakṣaṇaś ca sumantraś ca bāḍham ity eva rāghavam uktvā tam iṅgudīvṛkṣaṃ tadopayayatur hayaiḥ
english: Both Lakṣmaṇa and Sumantra replied "So be it" to Rāghava, and thereupon drove the horses up to that iṅgudī tree.

sanskrit: rāmo 'bhiyāya taṃ ramyaṃ vṛkṣam ikṣvākunandanaḥ rathād avātarat tasmāt sabhāryaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Rāma, that joy of the Ikṣvāku line, approached that lovely tree and descended from the chariot together with his wife and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: sumantro 'py avatīryaiva mocayitvā hayottamān vṛkṣamūlagataṃ rāmam upatasthe kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Sumantra too alighted, and having unharnessed those excellent horses, stood before Rāma who had seated himself at the foot of the tree, with hands joined in reverence.

sanskrit: tatra rājā guho nāma rāmasyātmasamaḥ sakhā niṣādajātyo balavān sthapatiś ceti viśrutaḥ
english: There lived a king named Guha, a dear friend of Rāma and equal to him in spirit, born of the Niṣāda people, powerful, and renowned as the lord of that territory.

sanskrit: sa śrutvā puruṣavyāghraṃ rāmaṃ viṣayam āgatam vṛddhaiḥ parivṛto 'mātyair jñātibhiś cāpy upāgataḥ
english: Hearing that Rāma, that tiger among men, had arrived in his territory, he came forward surrounded by his elders, ministers, and kinsmen.

sanskrit: tato niṣādādhipatiṃ dṛṣṭvā dūrād avasthitam saha saumitriṇā rāmaḥ samāgacchad guhena saḥ
english: Seeing the lord of the Niṣādas standing at a distance, Rāma together with Saumitri went forward and met with Guha.

sanskrit: tam ārtaḥ saṃpariṣvajya guho rāghavam abravīt yathāyodhyā tathedaṃ te rāma kiṃ karavāṇi te
english: Guha, filled with grief, embraced Rāghava and said: "Rāma, this land is as Ayodhyā to you — what may I do for you?"

sanskrit: tato guṇavadannādyam upādāya pṛthagvidham arghyaṃ copānayat kṣipraṃ vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha
english: Then, having gathered food and eatables of excellent quality in great variety, he quickly brought the honorific offering of arghya as well, and spoke these words:

sanskrit: svāgataṃ te mahābāho taveyam akhilā mahī vayaṃ preṣyā bhavān bhartā sādhu rājyaṃ praśādhi naḥ
english: "Welcome, O mighty-armed one! This whole earth is yours; we are your servants and you are our lord — graciously rule over our kingdom."

sanskrit: bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca peyaṃ ca lehyaṃ cedam upasthitam śayanāni ca mukhyāni vājināṃ khādanaṃ ca te
english: "Food to chew, food to eat, drink, and things to lick — all stand ready; and the finest beds are prepared, and fodder for your horses."

sanskrit: guham eva bruvāṇaṃ taṃ rāghavaḥ pratyuvāca ha arcitāś caiva hṛṣṭāś ca bhavatā sarvathā vayam
english: To Guha as he was still speaking, Rāghava replied: "We are honored and gladdened by you in every way."

sanskrit: padbhyām abhigamāc caiva snehasaṃdarśanena ca bhujābhyāṃ sādhuvṛttābhyāṃ pīḍayan vākyam abravīt
english: Squeezing him with both his well-formed arms — both on account of his coming on foot and as a display of affection — he spoke these words:

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tvāṃ guha paśyāmi arogaṃ saha bāndhavaiḥ api te kūśalaṃ rāṣṭre mitreṣu ca dhaneṣu ca
english: "It is my good fortune to see you, Guha, in good health together with your kinsmen. Is all well with you in your kingdom, among your friends and in your wealth?"

sanskrit: yat tv idaṃ bhavatā kiṃ cit prītyā samupakalpitam sarvaṃ tad anujānāmi na hi varte pratigrahe
english: "As for all that you have prepared out of affection, I accept it — yet I do not stand in need of receiving gifts."

sanskrit: kuśacīrājinadharaṃ phalamūlāśanaṃ ca mām viddhi praṇihitaṃ dharme tāpasaṃ vanagocaram
english: "Know me to be one who wears kuśa grass and bark-cloth garments, who subsists on fruits and roots, devoted to dharma, an ascetic whose range is the forest."

sanskrit: aśvānāṃ khādanenāham arthī nānyena kena cit etāvatātrabhavatā bhaviṣyāmi supūjitaḥ
english: "I desire nothing but fodder for the horses — by this much alone shall I be well honored by your good self."

sanskrit: ete hi dayitā rājñaḥ pitur daśarathasya me etaiḥ suvihitair aśvair bhaviṣyāmy aham arcitaḥ
english: "For these horses are beloved to the king, to my father Daśaratha — by having these horses well cared for shall I be truly honored."

sanskrit: aśvānāṃ pratipānaṃ ca khādanaṃ caiva so 'nvaśāt guhas tatraiva puruṣāṃs tvaritaṃ dīyatām iti
english: Guha then straightway commanded his men right there: "Let both water and fodder for the horses be brought at once!"

sanskrit: tataś cīrottarāsaṅgaḥ saṃdhyāṃ anvāsya paścimām jalam evādade bhojyaṃ lakṣmaṇenāhṛtaṃ svayam
english: Then, with his upper garment of bark-cloth, having duly attended the evening twilight rite, he took only water as his meal — the food was fetched by Lakṣmaṇa himself.

sanskrit: tasya bhūmau śayānasya pādau prakṣālya lakṣmaṇaḥ sabhāryasya tato 'bhyetya tasthau vṛkṣam upāśritaḥ
english: As he lay upon the ground together with his wife, Lakṣmaṇa washed his feet, and then, drawing near, stood leaning against the tree.

sanskrit: guho 'pi saha sūtena saumitrim anubhāṣayan anvajāgrat tato rāmam apramatto dhanurdharaḥ
english: Guha too, together with the charioteer, conversing with Saumitri, kept vigilant watch over Rāma through the night, bow in hand and alert.

sanskrit: tathā śayānasya tato 'sya dhīmato yaśasvino dāśarather mahātmanaḥ adṛṣṭaduḥkhasya sukhocitasya sā tadā vyatīyāya cireṇa śarvarī
english: Thus, as that wise and glorious great-souled son of Daśaratha lay resting — he who had never known suffering, accustomed to comfort — that night passed slowly away.

sanskrit: taṃ jāgratam adambhena bhrātur arthāya lakṣmaṇam guhaḥ saṃtāpasaṃtapto rāghavaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Guha, burning with anguish, spoke to Rāghava — addressing Lakṣmaṇa, who kept watch without pretense for the sake of his brother:

sanskrit: iyaṃ tāta sukhā śayyā tvadartham upakalpitā pratyāśvasihi sādhv asyāṃ rājaputra yathāsukham
english: "Dear friend, this comfortable bed has been prepared for your sake — rest well upon it, O prince, at your ease."

sanskrit: ucito 'yaṃ janaḥ sarvaḥ kleśānāṃ tvaṃ sukhocitaḥ guptyarthaṃ jāgariṣyāmaḥ kākutsthasya vayaṃ niśām
english: "All these people are accustomed to hardship; it is you who are accustomed to comfort. We shall keep watch through the night for the protection of Kākutstha."

sanskrit: na hi rāmāt priyataro mamāsti bhuvi kaś cana bravīmy etad ahaṃ satyaṃ satyenaiva ca te śape
english: "There is no one on earth dearer to me than Rāma — I speak this truth, and by truth itself I swear it to you."

sanskrit: asya prasādād āśaṃse loke 'smin sumahad yaśaḥ dharmāvāptiṃ ca vipulām arthāvāptiṃ ca kevalām
english: "By his grace I hope for supreme fame in this world, for abundant attainment of dharma and for the sole attainment of wealth."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ priyasakhaṃ rāmaṃ śayānaṃ saha sītayā rakṣiṣyāmi dhanuṣpāṇiḥ sarvato jñātibhiḥ saha
english: "Therefore I shall guard my dear friend Rāma as he sleeps with Sītā, bow in hand, together with my kinsmen on all sides."

sanskrit: na hi me 'viditaṃ kiṃ cid vane 'smiṃś carataḥ sadā caturaṅgaṃ hy api balaṃ sumahat prasahemahi
english: "Nothing in this forest is unknown to me, who roam here constantly — indeed we could withstand even a very great fourfold army."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇas taṃ tadovāca rakṣyamāṇās tvayānagha nātra bhītā vayaṃ sarve dharmam evānupaśyatā
english: Lakṣmaṇa then replied to him: "Being guarded by you, O sinless one, who ever have dharma in view, we have nothing here to fear."

sanskrit: kathaṃ dāśarathau bhūmau śayāne saha sītayā śakyā nidrā mayā labdhuṃ jīvitaṃ vā sukhāni vā
english: "How could I obtain sleep, or life, or pleasures, when the son of Daśaratha lies upon the bare ground together with Sītā?"

sanskrit: yo na devāsuraiḥ sarvaiḥ śakyaḥ prasahituṃ yudhi taṃ paśya sukhasaṃviṣṭaṃ tṛṇeṣu saha sītayā
english: "Behold him who could not be overpowered in battle by all the gods and asuras together — now lying comfortably on the grass with Sītā."

sanskrit: yo mantra tapasā labdho vividhaiś ca pariśramaiḥ eko daśarathasyaiṣa putraḥ sadṛśalakṣaṇaḥ
english: "This one son of Daśaratha, who was obtained by sacred rites, austerities, and various efforts, possessing every auspicious mark — he alone."

sanskrit: asmin pravrajito rājā na ciraṃ vartayiṣyati vidhavā medinī nūnaṃ kṣipram eva bhaviṣyati
english: "With him gone into exile, the king will not live long — the earth will surely become widowed very soon."

sanskrit: vinadya sumahānādaṃ śrameṇoparatāḥ striyaḥ nirghoṣoparataṃ tāta manye rājaniveśanam
english: "The women, exhausted with weeping, having cried out with a great lament, have fallen silent — I believe the king's palace has grown quiet, dear friend."

sanskrit: kausalyā caiva rājā ca tathaiva jananī mama nāśaṃse yadi jīvanti sarve te śarvarīm imām
english: "Kausalyā, and the king, and likewise my own mother — I do not hope that all of them will survive this night."

sanskrit: jīved api hi me mātā śatrughnasyānvavekṣayā tad duḥkhaṃ yat tu kausalyā vīrasūr vinaśiṣyati
english: "My mother might yet live, sustained by care from Śatrughna — yet it is grief that Kausalyā, the mother of this hero, shall perish."

sanskrit: anuraktajanākīrṇā sukhālokapriyāvahā rājavyasanasaṃsṛṣṭā sā purī vinaśiṣyati
english: "That city, filled with devoted people, offering delight and joy to those who behold it, now touched by the calamity of the king, shall perish."

sanskrit: atikrāntam atikrāntam anavāpya manoratham rājye rāmam anikṣipya pitā me vinaśiṣyati
english: "Gone, utterly gone — without having fulfilled his heart's desire, without having installed Rāma in the kingdom, my father shall perish."

sanskrit: siddhārthāḥ pitaraṃ vṛttaṃ tasmin kāle hy upasthite pretakāryeṣu sarveṣu saṃskariṣyanti bhūmipam
english: "Those whose purpose is accomplished — when that hour arrives and the king has passed — shall perform all the funerary rites and consecrate the lord of the earth."

sanskrit: ramyacatvarasaṃsthānāṃ suvibhaktamahāpathām harmyaprāsādasaṃpannāṃ gaṇikāvaraśobhitām
english: "With its lovely squares and intersections, its great highways well laid out, adorned with palaces and mansions, graced by the finest of courtesans —"

sanskrit: rathāśvagajasaṃbādhāṃ tūryanādavināditām sarvakalyāṇasaṃpūrṇāṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākulām
english: "— thronged with chariots, horses, and elephants, resounding with the music of instruments, filled with every prosperity, and crowded with cheerful and well-fed people —"

sanskrit: ārāmodyānasaṃpannāṃ samājotsavaśālinīm sukhitā vicariṣyanti rājadhānīṃ pitur mama
english: "— rich with pleasure groves and gardens, distinguished by assemblies and festivals — may the happy ones roam through my father's royal capital."

sanskrit: api satyapratijñena sārdhaṃ kuśalinā vayam nivṛtte vanavāse 'sminn ayodhyāṃ praviśemahi
english: "May we too, safe and sound, enter Ayodhyā together with him of true vow, when this forest sojourn has come to its end."

sanskrit: paridevayamānasya duḥkhārtasya mahātmanaḥ tiṣṭhato rājaputrasya śarvarī sātyavartata
english: As the great-souled prince stood there, lamenting and stricken with grief, the night passed fully away.

sanskrit: tathā hi satyaṃ bruvati prajāhite narendraputre gurusauhṛdād guhaḥ mumoca bāṣpaṃ vyasanābhipīḍito jvarāturo nāga iva vyathāturaḥ
english: For as that prince, devoted to the welfare of his people, spoke thus truthfully, Guha, oppressed by calamity and burning with grief out of his deep affection for his master, shed tears — like an elephant tormented by pain.
